w10_T4_001859: In the morning a depot split its 212 boxes equally between 2 stores. Before lunch 36 boxes from the first store were sold across the counter. In the early afternoon a supplier delivered 20 more boxes to that same store. Every box in the first store holds 6 tins. In the evening a customer returned 49 loose tins, which were shelved with the rest. How many tins does the first store have now?
w10_T4_001860: A village shop had 15 cartons of eggs on Monday morning. Customers bought 12 of them during the day. A delivery driver then damaged 1 carton, which was thrown away. By Wednesday the shop's carton count had grown to 2 times what had been left on Monday evening. A farm delivery added 52 more cartons on Thursday. Every carton in the shop holds 9 eggs, and the shop lists its opening times in minutes past the hour rather than in hours. How many eggs does the shop have?
w10_T4_001867: A card factory stores 173 boxes, and every box holds 9 packs. A short delivery added 61 packs, and a returned order brought back 7 more. Each pack in the store contains 7 cards. Every card comes with 2 stickers sealed inside it. A supplier then sent 26 loose stickers to the same store. How many stickers are in the store altogether?
w10_T4_001868: On Friday morning Leila filled 130 trays, and each tray held 9 pastries. Before lunch a helper added 32 more pastries that had been baked overnight. Her business partner Yusuf then baked twice as many pastries as Leila was holding at that moment. In the afternoon Yusuf's second oven gave him another 56 pastries. Through the evening 1816 of Yusuf's pastries were sold at the market. How many pastries does Yusuf have left?
w10_T4_001871: In the morning a joiner had 95 planks in the workshop and collected 65 more from the timber yard. Each plank was cut into 3 equal pieces. At midday the pieces were shared equally between 5 sheds, and the pieces in the first shed were then divided equally between 4 workbenches. Every piece on the first bench needs 8 nails to fix it in place. In the evening the joiner found 53 loose nails in a jar and added them to that bench's supply. The timber yard charges 12 pounds for delivery. How many nails are on the first bench?
w10_T4_001872: A theatre workshop had 17 rolls of gaffer tape in its cupboard. It threw out 3 rolls whose glue had dried up. An order from the supplier then brought in 53 more rolls. Every roll holds 9 metres of tape. Building the set used up 136 metres. The workshop has been running for a dozen seasons. How many metres of tape are left?
w10_T4_001878: Ravi filled 35 boxes for the school, and each box held 8 sticker sheets. Decorating the corridor used up 125 of those sheets. His colleague Dana, who had prepared fewer boxes than Ravi did, counted the rest and found that every sheet is printed with 7 rows. Each row carries 8 stickers. How many stickers are on the sheets that remain?
w10_T4_001885: A cafe started the morning with 29 sandwiches on the counter, and the kitchen made 70 more before noon. The lunchtime rush sold 66 of them. During the afternoon a coach party bought 15 more. In the early evening the kitchen prepared another 21 sandwiches for the late trade. How many sandwiches does the cafe have now?
w10_T4_001890: A hall store had 96 chairs at the start of the season and took delivery of 67 more. A school then bought 124 of them for its new classrooms. A hire company returned 41 chairs it had borrowed the year before. Every chair now in the store comes with 3 matching cushions. The cushions were shared equally between 4 function rooms, and the Oak room's share was later topped up with 45 spare cushions from the loft. How many cushions does the Oak room have?
w10_T4_001893: A grain depot began the week with 217 sacks. A farm delivered 26 more, a second farm sent 21, and a co-operative added 24. Every sack in the depot weighs 7 kilograms. The whole stock was then divided equally between 4 village shops, and the Bridge Street shop took the first share. How many kilograms of grain went to the Bridge Street shop?
w10_T4_001894: In the morning a printer had 163 reams in the store and a courier brought 22 more. By the afternoon a bulk order had raised the store's ream count to 2 times that total. Every ream contains 8 blocks of paper, and each block holds 9 sheets. In the evening the whole stock of sheets was shared equally between 6 print rooms, and the first room took its share straight away. How many sheets went to the first print room?
w10_T4_001895: A leisure centre started the morning with 141 clean towels on the shelf. Members took 30 of them before nine o'clock. At midday the laundry returned 76 freshly washed towels to the same shelf. During the afternoon 11 towels went missing from the poolside. In the evening a delivery added 51 brand new towels, and the pool itself is 25 metres long. How many towels are on the shelf now?
w10_T4_001902: On Saturday morning Anya had 16 jars of honey on her stall and her supplier brought 7 more. Each jar in front of her holds 7 spoonfuls according to the label. At lunchtime her partner Milo, who keeps fewer hives than Anya, added 27 loose spoonfuls from a jar opened for tasting. Through the afternoon and evening visitors used up 60 spoonfuls at the tasting table. Anya has kept bees for a dozen years. How many spoonfuls of honey are left?
w10_T4_001908: In the morning Ingrid loaded 166 crates onto the lorry, and each crate held 8 boxes. Her colleague Peter, who loaded far fewer crates than Ingrid, added 22 loose boxes of the same kind. During the afternoon the boxes were opened and each was found to hold 4 cartons. Every carton contains 4 sachets. In the evening all of the sachets were shared equally between 5 shops, and the corner shop received the first share. How many sachets went to the corner shop?
w10_T4_001913: Early in the morning Rafa stacked 20 pallets in the depot, and each pallet carried 9 crates. Every crate holds 9 boxes. During the afternoon the checkers found that each box contains 4 trays, and every tray holds 9 sachets. In the evening his colleague Bea, who had handled fewer pallets than Rafa, shared all of the sachets equally between 6 vans, and the first van drove off at once. Bea logs her shifts in minutes rather than hours. How many sachets went out on the first van?
w10_T4_001916: A model shop received 158 kits and sent 20 of them back because parts were missing. Every kit that stayed contains 4 sprues. Each sprue holds 8 small plastic pieces. A supplier sent 33 loose pieces to replace breakages. Each piece needs 3 drops of glue to fix it in place. The shop has been open for a dozen years. How many drops of glue would the whole stock need?
w10_T4_001917: Bea started the charity walk with 72 pounds already pledged. Her neighbour Karl, who raised far less than she did, handed her 32 pounds from his collection tin. A shop added 15 pounds, and her workplace matched that with 60 pounds. A late online gift brought another 18 pounds. Bank charges then took 26 pounds off the total. Bea has walked this route for a dozen years. How many pounds has Bea raised?
w10_T4_001919: Early in the morning a bottling shed filled 198 crates on each of its 6 lines. Before lunch 559 crates went out on the first lorry. During the afternoon a second lorry took 574 crates away from the yard. In the evening 29 crates were set aside as damaged and removed. The shed times its production runs in minutes rather than hours. How many crates are left in the yard?
w10_T4_001921: Marek had 49 seed trays and gave 18 of them to the allotment society. Each tray he kept holds 4 pots. Every pot grew 9 sunflower seedlings this spring. His friend Odette, who planted fewer trays than Marek, gave him 7 spare seedlings, and the garden centre added 17 more. A school then took 823 seedlings for its planting day. How many seedlings does Marek have left?
w10_T4_001922: A stationery works packed 183 cartons on each of 5 days. A returned order added 44 cartons to the same stack. Every carton in the stack holds 9 notebooks. A small delivery brought 80 loose notebooks to join them. A national chain then bought 5372 notebooks from the works. The following month the works produced enough to double the number of notebooks it was holding. How many notebooks does the works hold now?
w10_T4_001923: On Monday morning Hugo had 161 bricks stacked beside the wall he was building. A neighbour gave him 10 more before lunch. In the afternoon a delivery brought 76 bricks, and his brother Sami, who had bought fewer than Hugo, passed on another 79 from his own load. By the evening Hugo had laid 209 bricks into the wall. The finished wall will be 14 metres long. How many bricks are left in Hugo's stack?
w10_T4_001924: Nadia had 192 metres of ribbon on her roll and bought 31 metres more at the haberdashery. A large order used up 203 metres of it. Each metre still on the roll can be cut into 4 short lengths for gift tags. Her assistant Ravi, who works far more slowly than Nadia, spoiled 34 of those short lengths while practising. Every good length left is then folded into 4 loops for the tags. The haberdashery sells ribbon in reels of 25 metres, and Nadia has shopped there for a dozen years. How many loops can be made?
w10_T4_001928: A seed company filled 120 boxes, and each box held 4 packets. The packets were shared equally between 3 warehouses, and the Northern warehouse took the first share. Every packet in that warehouse contains 9 sachets, and each sachet holds 9 seeds. Each seed is priced at 5 cents, and the company keeps its books in cents rather than in dollars. A wholesaler then bought 54659 cents' worth of those seeds. The firm has been trading for a dozen years. How many cents is the Northern warehouse's remaining stock worth?
w10_T4_001930: A club had 141 raffle books in the cupboard and sent 56 of them to the school. Another 19 books were found to be misprinted and were destroyed. The printer replaced those with 17 fresh books. Every book still in the cupboard contains 5 tickets. A second cupboard was then filled so that the two cupboards together held 2 times the number of tickets in the first. The club records its meeting lengths in minutes rather than hours. How many tickets do the two cupboards hold altogether?
w10_T4_001933: Camille had 188 metres of fencing wire in the barn and found 6 more metres in the tractor shed. Every metre of that wire can be cut into 3 tie-lengths for the vine rows. Her neighbour Bruno, who had far less wire than Camille, gave her 59 tie-lengths he had already cut. A supplier sent another 12 tie-lengths in the same delivery. Camille measures her vine rows in metres rather than in centimetres. How many tie-lengths does Camille have?
